**1. Tính toán Calo:**

*   **Tính BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate - Tỷ lệ trao đổi chất cơ bản):** Sử dụng công thức Mifflin-St Jeor (thường được coi là chính xác hơn cho dân số hiện đại):
    BMR = (10 × cân nặng [kg]) + (6.25 × chiều cao [cm]) – (5 × tuổi [năm]) + 5 (cho nam)
    BMR = (10 × 110) + (6.25 × 168) – (5 × 34) + 5
    BMR = 1100 + 1050 – 170 + 5 = 1985 kcal
*   **Tính TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure - Tổng năng lượng tiêu thụ hàng ngày):**
    Với người làm văn phòng, ít vận động, hệ số vận động (Activity Factor - AF) thường là 1.2.
    TDEE = BMR × AF = 1985 × 1.2 = 2382 kcal/ngày

**2. Mục tiêu Calo để giảm cân:**

*   **Để giảm 20kg trong ~90 ngày:**
    Tổng calo cần thâm hụt = 20 kg × 7700 kcal/kg ≈ 154,000 kcal
    Mức thâm hụt hàng ngày = 154,000 kcal / 90 ngày ≈ 1711 kcal/ngày
    Lượng calo nạp vào mục tiêu = TDEE - Thâm hụt = 2382 - 1711 = 671 kcal/ngày.
    **Đây là mức calo cực kỳ thấp, không an toàn và không bền vững.**
*   **Mục tiêu thực tế hơn (giảm ~1kg/tuần):**

    Lượng calo nạp vào mục tiêu = TDEE - Thâm hụt = 2382 - 1100 = 1282 kcal/ngày.
    Để an toàn và dễ thực hiện hơn, có thể đặt mục tiêu khoảng **1500 kcal/ngày**, kết hợp với việc tăng cường vận động (đi bộ, bắt đầu tập gym nhẹ nhàng). Mức này sẽ giúp giảm khoảng 0.8-0.9 kg/tuần (khoảng 10-11kg trong 3 tháng) nếu chỉ dựa vào ăn kiêng, và nhiều hơn nếu kết hợp tập luyện.

*   **Carbohydrate (Tinh bột): 30%** (Cung cấp năng lượng, ưu tiên carb phức) = 1500 * 0.30 = 450 kcal = 112.5g
*   **Fat (Chất béo): 30%** (Cần thiết cho hormone, ưu tiên béo tốt) = 1500 * 0.30 = 450 kcal = 50g

Dưới đây là cách tính toán và một gợi ý meal plan mẫu cho nam thanh niên 34 tuổi, cao 1m68, nặng 110 kg, làm văn phòng và chưa tập gym với mục tiêu “giảm 20 kg trong 3 tháng”. Trước tiên, cần lưu ý rằng mục tiêu giảm cân nhanh (20 kg trong 3 tháng) khá tham vọng và có thể không an toàn nếu không có sự giám sát y tế, nên bạn nên cân nhắc điều chỉnh mục tiêu cho phù hợp. Dưới đây chỉ là ví dụ tham khảo dựa trên các công thức và giả định thông thường.

──────────────────────────────
1. TÍNH TOÁN CƠ BẢN

a. Tính BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate – lượng calo cần thiết khi nghỉ ngơi)  
Một công thức được sử dụng rộng rãi hiện nay là công thức Mifflin-St Jeor:  
  BMR = (10 × cân nặng [kg]) + (6.25 × chiều cao [cm]) – (5 × tuổi) + 5

Với số liệu:  
  Cân nặng: 110 kg  
  Chiều cao: 168 cm  
  Tuổi: 34  
→ BMR = (10 × 110) + (6.25 × 168) – (5 × 34) + 5  
     = 1100 + 1050 – 170 + 5  
     = 1985 kcal/ngày (xấp xỉ)

b. Tính TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure – tổng lượng calo tiêu hao hàng ngày)  
Với người làm văn phòng, mức độ hoạt động thường được đánh giá là “ít vận động” (sedenatry) và thường nhân với hệ số khoảng 1.2:  
  TDEE ≈ 1985 × 1.2 ≈ 2382 kcal/ngày

──────────────────────────────
2. MỤC TIÊU GIẢM CÂN

Giảm 20 kg trong 3 tháng (tương đương ≈12 tuần) nghĩa là giảm trung bình khoảng 1.67 kg mỗi tuần.  
• Lượng calo cần giảm để mất 1 kg mỡ xấp xỉ 7700 kcal.  
  Do đó, mỗi tuần cần tạo thâm hụt: 1.67 × 7700 ≈ 12,860 kcal  
  Thâm hụt cần thiết mỗi ngày ≈ 12,860 / 7 ≈ 1837 kcal

So với TDEE ≈2382 kcal/ngày, nếu chỉ dùng hạn chế chế độ ăn mà không tập thể dục, bạn sẽ cần ăn khoảng 2382 – 1837 ≈ 545 kcal/ngày – con số này quá thấp và không an toàn.

Do đó, hầu hết chuyên gia khuyến nghị giảm cân an toàn thường hướng đến thâm hụt từ 500 đến 1000 kcal/ngày (tương đương giảm khoảng 0.5–1 kg mỗi tuần). Để đạt mục tiêu giảm 20 kg trong 3 tháng, cần kết hợp giữa chế độ ăn kiêng nghiêm ngặt và tăng cường hoạt động thể chất (tập gym, đi bộ, …) dưới sự theo dõi của chuyên gia.

Trong ví dụ này, chúng ta sẽ đưa ra một meal plan mẫu dựa trên mục tiêu ăn khoảng 1500 kcal/ngày. Với TDEE khoảng 2382 kcal, chế độ 1500 kcal đem lại thâm hụt khoảng 882 kcal/ngày. Mức này có thể dẫn đến giảm khoảng 0.8 kg mỗi tuần, tương đương ~10 kg trong 12 tuần. Việc giảm 20 kg yêu cầu thâm hụt sâu hơn – thường phải có sự kết hợp giữa ăn kiêng và tập luyện tăng cường vận động. (Với mục tiêu giảm nhanh, bạn phải thận trọng và có thể cần bổ sung tập luyện cường độ cao, tham vấn bác sĩ/din hạnh để tránh ảnh hưởng đến sức khỏe.)

──────────────────────────────
3. PHÂN BỔ MACROS (cho 1500 kcal/ngày – là ví dụ tham khảo)

Một tỉ lệ phân chia macros hợp lý có thể là:  
• Protein: ~30%  
• Carbohydrate: ~40%  
• Fat: ~30%

Tính ra:  
• Calories từ Protein: 1500 × 0.30 = 450 kcal → ≈450/4 = 112 g protein  
• Calories từ Carbs: 1500 × 0.40 = 600 kcal → ≈600/4 = 150 g carbs  
• Calories từ Fat: 1500 × 0.30 = 450 kcal → ≈450/9 = 50 g fat

──────────────────────────────
4. MEAL PLAN MẪU (1500 kcal/ngày)

Lưu ý: Các con số dưới đây chỉ mang tính ước tính, bạn có thể điều chỉnh thực đơn theo khẩu vị, nhu cầu dinh dưỡng, và thời gian trong ngày. Hơn nữa, nếu có thể kết hợp tập luyện thi đua, bạn có thể tăng mức thâm hụt an toàn hơn.

SÁNG (Khoảng 7:00 – 8:00)

• (Tổng ~350 kcal, ~25 g protein, 45 g carbs, 10 g fat)

BỮA PHỤ GIỎI (Giữa buổi sáng, khoảng 10:00)

TRƯA (Khoảng 12:00 – 13:00)

TỐI (Khoảng 19:00 – 20:00)

(Tổng cộng xấp xỉ 1450–1500 kcal/ngày với macros gần đúng: ~112–120 g protein, ~150 g carbs, ~50 g fat)

──────────────────────────────
5. LƯU Ý CHUNG

• Nếu bạn muốn đạt mục tiêu giảm 20 kg trong 3 tháng, cần cân nhắc việc tăng hoạt động thể chất: ví dụ, thêm bài tập gym, đi bộ nhanh, tập HIIT,… để tăng lượng calo tiêu hao.

• Hãy luôn uống đủ nước và chú ý cân bằng dinh dưỡng; không nên bỏ bữa hoặc thuêt sức.  
• Tốt nhất, hãy tham vấn chuyên gia dinh dưỡng/luyện tập để có chế độ phù hợp với thể trạng và nhu cầu của cơ thể bạn.

Hy vọng với cách tính toán và meal plan mẫu này, bạn sẽ có định hướng để xây dựng chế độ ăn – tập phù hợp cho mục tiêu giảm cân của mình. Chúc bạn thành công và khỏe mạnh!

Okay, let's break this down.

**My Answer:**

1.  **Calculate BMR and TDEE:**
    *   Using the Mifflin-St Jeor formula (generally considered more accurate for modern populations, especially overweight individuals):
        *   BMR = (10 * weight_kg) + (6.25 * height_cm) - (5 * age) + 5
        *   BMR = (10 * 110) + (6.25 * 168) - (5 * 34) + 5
        *   BMR = 1100 + 1050 - 170 + 5 = 1985 kcal
    *   Activity Level: Sedentary (office work, no gym) = Activity Factor 1.2
    *   TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) = BMR * Activity Factor
    *   TDEE = 1985 * 1.2 = 2382 kcal/day

2.  **Evaluate Goal Feasibility (Lose 20kg in 3 months):**
    *   3 months ≈ 90 days.
    *   To lose 1 kg of fat requires a deficit of approximately 7700 kcal.
    *   Total deficit needed = 20 kg * 7700 kcal/kg = 154,000 kcal.
    *   Required daily deficit = 154,000 kcal / 90 days ≈ 1711 kcal/day.
    *   Required daily calorie intake = TDEE - Daily Deficit = 2382 - 1711 = 671 kcal/day.
    *   **WARNING:** This (671 kcal/day) is dangerously low, unsustainable, likely to cause muscle loss, nutrient deficiencies, metabolic damage, and health problems. The goal of losing 20kg in 3 months is extremely aggressive and generally unsafe, especially without professional medical and nutritional supervision and significant exercise incorporation.
    *   **Realistic Adjustment:** A safe and sustainable rate of weight loss is typically 0.5-1 kg per week (a deficit of 500-1000 kcal/day). Let's aim for a ~900 kcal deficit per day (~1 kg/week loss).
    *   Adjusted Calorie Target = TDEE - 900 = 2382 - 900 = 1482 kcal/day. Let's round to **1500 kcal/day**. This would realistically lead to about 11-12 kg loss over 3 months, which is still significant but much safer.

3.  **Macronutrient Split (for 1500 kcal/day):**

**My Answer:**

The user wants to prove that the expression n⁴ - 4n is divisible by 5 for all integers (or natural numbers) n. The prompt is in Armenian: "Ապացուցել, որ n^4_4n բաժանվում է 5_ի".

First, let's check if the statement is true by testing values of n modulo 5. Let f(n) = n⁴ - 4n.

1.  **Case n ≡ 0 (mod 5):**
    f(n) ≡ 0⁴ - 4(0) = 0 (mod 5). The statement holds.
2.  **Case n ≡ 1 (mod 5):**
    f(n) ≡ 1⁴ - 4(1) = 1 - 4 = -3 ≡ 2 (mod 5). The statement does not hold.
3.  **Case n ≡ 2 (mod 5):**
    f(n) ≡ 2⁴ - 4(2) = 16 - 8 = 8 ≡ 3 (mod 5). The statement does not hold.
4.  **Case n ≡ 3 (mod 5):**
    f(n) ≡ 3⁴ - 4(3) = 81 - 12 = 69 ≡ 4 (mod 5). The statement does not hold.
5.  **Case n ≡ 4 (mod 5):**
    f(n) ≡ 4⁴ - 4(4) = 256 - 16 = 240. Since 240 = 5 × 48, 240 ≡ 0 (mod 5). The statement holds.

**Conclusion:**
The statement "n⁴ - 4n is divisible by 5 for all n" is **false**. The expression n⁴ - 4n is divisible by 5 if and only if n ≡ 0 (mod 5) or n ≡ 4 (mod 5).

Therefore, it is impossible to prove the original statement as written because it is not universally true. The correct response is to demonstrate that it's false and identify the conditions under which it is true.

**(Answer in Armenian):**
Պնդումը, թե n⁴ - 4n արտահայտությունը միշտ բաժանվում է 5-ի ցանկացած n ամբողջ թվի համար, ճիշտ չէ։ Սա կարելի է ցույց տալ՝ ստուգելով n-ի հնարավոր մնացորդները 5-ի բաժանելիս։

Դիտարկենք n⁴ - 4n (mod 5)։
1.  Եթե n ≡ 0 (mod 5), ապա n⁴ - 4n ≡ 0⁴ - 4(0) = 0 (mod 5)։

**My Answer:**

**1. Interpretation:**
The crucial point is interpreting "Working capital needs are estimated to be 15% of net revenue... each year is as follows: Year 1: 1,100 million VND...". The most natural reading is that the listed numbers (1,100, 1,150, 1,200, 1,100) represent the *required working capital* (WC) balance at the *end* of each respective year (or equivalently, the WC needed *for* the following year's operations). Therefore, revenue must be calculated from these WC figures. Standard practice also dictates that the working capital needed for Year 1 is typically invested at the beginning of the project (t=0).

**2. Calculate Net Revenue (R):**
Since WC = 0.15 * R, then R = WC / 0.15.
*   R₁ = 1100 / 0.15 ≈ 7333.33 million VND
*   R₂ = 1150 / 0.15 ≈ 7666.67 million VND
*   R₃ = 1200 / 0.15 = 8000.00 million VND
*   R₄ = 1100 / 0.15 ≈ 7333.33 million VND

**3. Calculate Annual Depreciation:**
Straight-line depreciation = Fixed Asset Cost / Useful Life = 500 / 4 = 125 million VND per year.

**4. Calculate Annual Operating Cash Flow (OCF):**
OCF = (Revenue - Variable Costs - Fixed Costs - Depreciation) * (1 - Tax Rate) + Depreciation
OCF = (R - 0.70*R - 100 - 125) * (1 - 0.20) + 125
OCF = (0.30*R - 225) * 0.80 + 125
*   OCF₁ = (0.30 * 7333.33 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = (2200 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = 1975 * 0.80 + 125 = 1580 + 125 = 1705
*   OCF₂ = (0.30 * 7666.67 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = (2300 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = 2075 * 0.80 + 125 = 1660 + 125 = 1785
*   OCF₃ = (0.30 * 8000.00 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = (2400 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = 2175 * 0.80 + 125 = 1740 + 125 = 1865
*   OCF₄ = (0.30 * 7333.33 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = (2200 - 225) * 0.80 + 125 = 1975 * 0.80 + 125 = 1580 + 125 = 1705

**5. Calculate Changes in Working Capital (ΔWC):**
Assuming WC needed *for* Year N is invested at the *start* of Year N (i.e., end of Year N-1 or t=N-1).
*   WC Required (End of Year):
    *   t=0: 1100 (for Year 1)
    *   t=1: 1150 (for Year 2)
    *   t=2: 1200 (for Year 3)
    *   t=3: 1100 (for Year 4)
    *   t=4: 0 (Project ends, WC recovered)

    *   t=3: -(1100 - 1200) = +100
    *   t=4: -(0 - 1100) = +1100 (Full recovery of the balance at end of Year 3)

**6. Calculate Net Cash Flow (NCF):**
NCF = OCF + ΔWC + Initial Fixed Asset Investment (at t=0)
*   NCF₀ = -500 (Fixed Assets) - 1100 (Initial WC) = -1600
*   NCF₁ = OCF₁ + ΔWC₁ = 1705 - 50 = 1655
*   NCF₂ = OCF₂ + ΔWC₂ = 1785 - 50 = 1735
*   NCF₃ = OCF₃ + ΔWC₃ = 1865 + 100 = 1965
*   NCF₄ = OCF₄ + ΔWC₄ = 1705 + 1100 = 2805

**7. Calculate NPV:**

NPV = Σ [NCFₜ / (1 + k)ᵗ] for t = 0 to 4
NPV = -1600 / (1.12)⁰ + 1655 / (1.12)¹ + 1735 / (1.12)² + 1965 / (1.12)³ + 2805 / (1.12)⁴

Below is one worked‐example showing one way to “solve” this type of problem. In our case the firm is planning on spending 500 million VND for fixed assets, and it must “tie up” working capital each year. (In our solution we assume that the working capital requirements are “built‐up” gradually so that the change from one year to the next is what matters, with the full working capital then “released” at the end of the project.) We also use the fact that – by assumption – net revenue “drives” several items (variable costs and the working‐capital requirement). One common interpretation of the wording is to “back out” the revenue numbers from the working capital statement. (That is, if working capital equals 15% of revenue, and if you are told that in Year 1 working capital is 1,100 million VND then revenue must have been about 1,100/0.15.) One acceptable answer is as follows.

──────────────────────────────
Step 1. Determine “Gross” (net) revenue in each year

We are told that the working capital requirement in each year equals 15% of net revenue. Thus, if we denote annual net revenue by R then
  WC = 0.15 × R  ⇒  R = WC/0.15.
For each year we obtain:
 Year 1: R₁ = 1,100/0.15 ≈ 7,333 million VND
 Year 2: R₂ = 1,150/0.15 ≈ 7,667 million VND
 Year 3: R₃ = 1,200/0.15 = 8,000 million VND
 Year 4: R₄ = 1,100/0.15 ≈ 7,333 million VND

──────────────────────────────
Step 2. Compute Operating Costs and Depreciation

The project has two kinds of operating expenses:
• Variable costs are 70% of net revenue.
• Fixed costs (other than depreciation) are 100 million VND/year.

Also, the fixed assets cost 500 million VND and are depreciated straight‐line over 4 years (salvage is negligible). Therefore, annual depreciation = 500/4 = 125 million VND per year.

Let’s list the computations year‐by‐year.

For Year i use:
 Revenue = Rᵢ
 Variable Costs = 0.70 Rᵢ
 Fixed Operating Costs = 100
 Depreciation = 125

Thus EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) is:
 EBIT = Rᵢ – (0.70 Rᵢ) – 100 – 125
    = 0.30 Rᵢ – 225

Now calculate for each year:

• Year 1: 
 R₁ ≈ 7,333 
 Variable costs ≈ 0.70×7,333 ≈ 5,133 
 ⇒ EBIT₁ = 0.30×7,333 – 225 ≈ 2,200 – 225 = 1,975 million VND

• Year 2:
 R₂ ≈ 7,667 
 Variable costs ≈ 0.70×7,667 ≈ 5,367 
 ⇒ EBIT₂ = 0.30×7,667 – 225 ≈ 2,300 – 225 = 2,075 million VND

• Year 3:
 R₃ = 8,000 
 Variable costs = 0.70×8,000 = 5,600 
 ⇒ EBIT₃ = 0.30×8,000 – 225 = 2,400 – 225 = 2,175 million VND

• Year 4:
 R₄ ≈ 7,333 
 Variable costs ≈ 5,133 
 ⇒ EBIT₄ = 0.30×7,333 – 225 ≈ 2,200 – 225 = 1,975 million VND

The income‐tax rate is 20%, so:
 Tax = 0.20 × EBIT

Thus:
 Year 1 Tax = 0.20×1,975 = 395  
 Year 2 Tax = 0.20×2,075 = 415  
 Year 3 Tax = 0.20×2,175 = 435  
 Year 4 Tax = 0.20×1,975 = 395  

After‐tax operating income = EBIT – Tax.
Then, because depreciation is a non‐cash charge we add it back to get the operating cash flow (OCF).

So:
 OCF = (EBIT – Tax) + Depreciation

Compute each year:
• Year 1: OCF₁ = (1,975 – 395) + 125 = 1,580 + 125 = 1,705 million VND  
• Year 2: OCF₂ = (2,075 – 415) + 125 = 1,660 + 125 = 1,785 million VND  
• Year 3: OCF₃ = (2,175 – 435) + 125 = 1,740 + 125 = 1,865 million VND  
• Year 4: OCF₄ = (1,975 – 395) + 125 = 1,580 + 125 = 1,705 million VND  

──────────────────────────────
Step 3. Determine Working Capital Investments

Because the working capital is 15% of revenue, the “required” working capital at the end of each year is given. However, cash flows come from the changes in working capital. Define WC₀ = 0 at project start and then:
 WC₁ = 1,100  
 WC₂ = 1,150  
 WC₃ = 1,200  
 WC₄ = 1,100

So the incremental (year‐to‐year) changes are:
 Year 1: ΔWC₁ = 1,100 – 0 = 1,100   (investment, so cash outflow)
 Year 2: ΔWC₂ = 1,150 – 1,100 = 50   (additional investment)
 Year 3: ΔWC₃ = 1,200 – 1,150 = 50   (additional investment)
 Year 4: ΔWC₄ = 1,100 – 1,200 = –100  (a partial release during Year 4)

Also, “fully recovered at the end” means that at the project’s termination the remaining working capital of 1,100 million VND is retrieved (cash inflow).

──────────────────────────────
Step 4. Form the Total Cash Flow Schedule

Time 0 (t = 0):
 • Fixed asset investment: –500 million VND
 • (We assume no WC cash flow at t = 0; the first WC investment is made at the end of Year 1.)

Year 1 (t = 1):
 • OCF₁ = 1,705
 • Additional WC investment: –1,100  
 Net CF₁ = 1,705 – 1,100 = 605 million VND

Year 2 (t = 2):
 • OCF₂ = 1,785  
 • Additional WC investment: –50  
 Net CF₂ = 1,785 – 50 = 1,735 million VND

Year 3 (t = 3):
 • OCF₃ = 1,865  
 • Additional WC investment: –50  
 Net CF₃ = 1,865 – 50 = 1,815 million VND

Year 4 (t = 4):
 • OCF₄ = 1,705  
 • The change in WC this year gives an inflow of 100 (since WC drops by 100 compared to Year 3)  
 • At the end of the project the entire remaining WC (1,100) is recovered.
 Net CF₄ = 1,705 + 100 + 1,100 = 2,905 million VND

──────────────────────────────
Step 5. Discount the Cash Flows at the 12% Cost of Capital

Our discount factors are:
 Year 0: 1
 Year 1: 1/(1.12) ≈ 0.8929
 Year 2: 1/(1.12²) ≈ 0.7972  (1/1.2544)
 Year 3: 1/(1.12³) ≈ 0.7118  (1/1.4049)
 Year 4: 1/(1.12⁴) ≈ 0.6355  (1/1.5735)

Now, NPV = (–500)
       + (605 × 0.8929)
       + (1,735 × 0.7972)
       + (1,815 × 0.7118)
       + (2,905 × 0.6355)

Let’s compute:
• Year 1 PV = 605 × 0.8929 ≈ 540.2
• Year 2 PV = 1,735 × 0.7972 ≈ 1,384.1
• Year 3 PV = 1,815 × 0.7118 ≈ 1,292.3
• Year 4 PV = 2,905 × 0.6355 ≈ 1,846.7

Summing these:
 Total PV = –500 + 540.2 + 1,384.1 + 1,292.3 + 1,846.7  
        = –500 + (540.2 + 1,384.1) + (1,292.3 + 1,846.7)
        = –500 + 1,924.3 + 3,139.0  
        = 4,563.3 million VND (approximately)

──────────────────────────────
Step 6. Conclusion

The net present value (NPV) of the project is about 4,563 million VND. (Some rounding is involved.)

──────────────────────────────
Notes:

1. The “reverse‐engineering” of revenue from the working capital requirement relies on the statement that WC is 15% of net revenue.
2. The working capital cash flows are taken as the changes year‐to‐year plus a full recovery at the end.
3. All amounts are in millions of VND.
4. The cost of capital is 12% per year.

Any answer that follows a logic equivalent to the above (perhaps with slight differences in timing assumptions for working capital) would be acceptable.

──────────────────────────────
Final Answer:

The NPV of the project is approximately 4,560–4,570 million VND (roughly 4.56 billion VND).

Below is one worked‐example showing one way to “solve” this type of problem. In our case the firm is planning on spending 500 million VND for fixed assets, and it must “tie up” working capital each year. (In our solution we assume that the working capital requirements are “built‐up” gradually so that the change from one year to the next is what matters, with the full working capital then “released” at the end of the project.) We also use the fact that – by assumption – net revenue “drives” several items (variable costs and the working‐capital requirement). One common interpretation of the wording is to “back out” the revenue numbers from the working capital statement. (That is, if working capital equals 15% of revenue, and if you are told that in Year 1 working capital is 1,100 million VND then revenue must have been about 1,100/0.15.) One acceptable answer is as follows.

──────────────────────────────
Step 1. Determine “Gross” (net) revenue in each year

We are told that the working capital requirement in each year equals 15% of net revenue. Thus, if we denote annual net revenue by R then
  WC = 0.15 × R  ⇒  R = WC/0.15.
For each year we obtain:
 Year 1: R₁ = 1,100/0.15 ≈ 7,333 million VND
 Year 2: R₂ = 1,150/0.15 ≈ 7,667 million VND
 Year 3: R₃ = 1,200/0.15 = 8,000 million VND
 Year 4: R₄ = 1,100/0.15 ≈ 7,333 million VND

──────────────────────────────
Step 2. Compute Operating Costs and Depreciation

The project has two kinds of operating expenses:
• Variable costs are 70% of net revenue.
• Fixed costs (other than depreciation) are 100 million VND/year.

Also, the fixed assets cost 500 million VND and are depreciated straight‐line over 4 years (salvage is negligible). Therefore, annual depreciation = 500/4 = 125 million VND per year.

Let’s list the computations year‐by‐year.

For Year i use:
 Revenue = Rᵢ
 Variable Costs = 0.70 Rᵢ
 Fixed Operating Costs = 100
 Depreciation = 125

Thus EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) is:
 EBIT = Rᵢ – (0.70 Rᵢ) – 100 – 125
    = 0.30 Rᵢ – 225

Now calculate for each year:

• Year 1: 
 R₁ ≈ 7,333 
 Variable costs ≈ 0.70×7,333 ≈ 5,133 
 ⇒ EBIT₁ = 0.30×7,333 – 225 ≈ 2,200 – 225 = 1,975 million VND

• Year 2:
 R₂ ≈ 7,667 
 Variable costs ≈ 0.70×7,667 ≈ 5,367 
 ⇒ EBIT₂ = 0.30×7,667 – 225 ≈ 2,300 – 225 = 2,075 million VND

• Year 3:
 R₃ = 8,000 
 Variable costs = 0.70×8,000 = 5,600 
 ⇒ EBIT₃ = 0.30×8,000 – 225 = 2,400 – 225 = 2,175 million VND

• Year 4:
 R₄ ≈ 7,333 
 Variable costs ≈ 5,133 
 ⇒ EBIT₄ = 0.30×7,333 – 225 ≈ 2,200 – 225 = 1,975 million VND

The income‐tax rate is 20%, so:
 Tax = 0.20 × EBIT

Thus:
 Year 1 Tax = 0.20×1,975 = 395  
 Year 2 Tax = 0.20×2,075 = 415  
 Year 3 Tax = 0.20×2,175 = 435  
 Year 4 Tax = 0.20×1,975 = 395  

After‐tax operating income = EBIT – Tax.
Then, because depreciation is a non‐cash charge we add it back to get the operating cash flow (OCF).

So:
 OCF = (EBIT – Tax) + Depreciation

Compute each year:
• Year 1: OCF₁ = (1,975 – 395) + 125 = 1,580 + 125 = 1,705 million VND  
• Year 2: OCF₂ = (2,075 – 415) + 125 = 1,660 + 125 = 1,785 million VND  
• Year 3: OCF₃ = (2,175 – 435) + 125 = 1,740 + 125 = 1,865 million VND  
• Year 4: OCF₄ = (1,975 – 395) + 125 = 1,580 + 125 = 1,705 million VND  

──────────────────────────────
Step 3. Determine Working Capital Investments

Because the working capital is 15% of revenue, the “required” working capital at the end of each year is given. However, cash flows come from the changes in working capital. Define WC₀ = 0 at project start and then:
 WC₁ = 1,100  
 WC₂ = 1,150  
 WC₃ = 1,200  
 WC₄ = 1,100

So the incremental (year‐to‐year) changes are:
 Year 1: ΔWC₁ = 1,100 – 0 = 1,100   (investment, so cash outflow)
 Year 2: ΔWC₂ = 1,150 – 1,100 = 50   (additional investment)
 Year 3: ΔWC₃ = 1,200 – 1,150 = 50   (additional investment)
 Year 4: ΔWC₄ = 1,100 – 1,200 = –100  (a partial release during Year 4)

Also, “fully recovered at the end” means that at the project’s termination the remaining working capital of 1,100 million VND is retrieved (cash inflow).

──────────────────────────────
Step 4. Form the Total Cash Flow Schedule

Time 0 (t = 0):
 • Fixed asset investment: –500 million VND
 • (We assume no WC cash flow at t = 0; the first WC investment is made at the end of Year 1.)

Year 1 (t = 1):
 • OCF₁ = 1,705
 • Additional WC investment: –1,100  
 Net CF₁ = 1,705 – 1,100 = 605 million VND

Year 2 (t = 2):
 • OCF₂ = 1,785  
 • Additional WC investment: –50  
 Net CF₂ = 1,785 – 50 = 1,735 million VND

Year 3 (t = 3):
 • OCF₃ = 1,865  
 • Additional WC investment: –50  
 Net CF₃ = 1,865 – 50 = 1,815 million VND

Year 4 (t = 4):
 • OCF₄ = 1,705  
 • The change in WC this year gives an inflow of 100 (since WC drops by 100 compared to Year 3)  
 • At the end of the project the entire remaining WC (1,100) is recovered.
 Net CF₄ = 1,705 + 100 + 1,100 = 2,905 million VND

──────────────────────────────
Step 5. Discount the Cash Flows at the 12% Cost of Capital

Our discount factors are:
 Year 0: 1
 Year 1: 1/(1.12) ≈ 0.8929
 Year 2: 1/(1.12²) ≈ 0.7972  (1/1.2544)
 Year 3: 1/(1.12³) ≈ 0.7118  (1/1.4049)
 Year 4: 1/(1.12⁴) ≈ 0.6355  (1/1.5735)

Now, NPV = (–500)
       + (605 × 0.8929)
       + (1,735 × 0.7972)
       + (1,815 × 0.7118)
       + (2,905 × 0.6355)

Let’s compute:
• Year 1 PV = 605 × 0.8929 ≈ 540.2
• Year 2 PV = 1,735 × 0.7972 ≈ 1,384.1
• Year 3 PV = 1,815 × 0.7118 ≈ 1,292.3
• Year 4 PV = 2,905 × 0.6355 ≈ 1,846.7

Summing these:
 Total PV = –500 + 540.2 + 1,384.1 + 1,292.3 + 1,846.7  
        = –500 + (540.2 + 1,384.1) + (1,292.3 + 1,846.7)
        = –500 + 1,924.3 + 3,139.0  
        = 4,563.3 million VND (approximately)

──────────────────────────────
Step 6. Conclusion

The net present value (NPV) of the project is about 4,563 million VND. (Some rounding is involved.)

──────────────────────────────
Notes:

1. The “reverse‐engineering” of revenue from the working capital requirement relies on the statement that WC is 15% of net revenue.
2. The working capital cash flows are taken as the changes year‐to‐year plus a full recovery at the end.
3. All amounts are in millions of VND.
4. The cost of capital is 12% per year.

Any answer that follows a logic equivalent to the above (perhaps with slight differences in timing assumptions for working capital) would be acceptable.

──────────────────────────────
Final Answer:

The NPV of the project is approximately 4,560–4,570 million VND (roughly 4.56 billion VND).
<|The End of Assistant B's Answer|>

**My Answer**

**Mục tiêu:** Tìm số lần tặng kẹo (m) lớn nhất có thể từ n chiếc kẹo, sao cho mỗi lần tặng ít nhất 1 kẹo, tổng số kẹo không vượt quá n, và số kẹo tặng ở hai lần liên tiếp phải khác nhau.

**Phân tích:**
Để tối đa hóa số lần tặng quà (m), Văn cần sử dụng số kẹo ít nhất có thể cho mỗi lần tặng, đồng thời tuân thủ các điều kiện. Số kẹo nhỏ nhất có thể tặng là 1. Tuy nhiên, không thể tặng 1 kẹo liên tiếp hai lần. Do đó, cách tối ưu để dùng ít kẹo nhất mà vẫn đảm bảo số kẹo ở hai lần liên tiếp khác nhau là tặng xen kẽ 1 và 2 kẹo.

Chuỗi tặng quà tối ưu sẽ là: 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, ...

**Tính tổng số kẹo cần dùng (T) cho m lần tặng theo chuỗi này:**
*   Nếu m là số lẻ (m = 2k + 1): Có (m+1)/2 lần tặng 1 kẹo và (m-1)/2 lần tặng 2 kẹo.
    Tổng T = 1 * [(m+1)/2] + 2 * [(m-1)/2] = (m+1 + 2m-2) / 2 = (3m - 1) / 2.
*   Nếu m là số chẵn (m = 2k): Có m/2 lần tặng 1 kẹo và m/2 lần tặng 2 kẹo.
    Tổng T = 1 * (m/2) + 2 * (m/2) = (m + 2m) / 2 = 3m / 2.

**Tìm m lớn nhất:**
Chúng ta cần tìm số nguyên m lớn nhất sao cho tổng số kẹo T không vượt quá n (T ≤ n).
*   Nếu m lẻ: (3m - 1) / 2 ≤ n  =>  3m - 1 ≤ 2n  =>  3m ≤ 2n + 1  =>  m ≤ (2n + 1) / 3.
*   Nếu m chẵn: 3m / 2 ≤ n  =>  3m ≤ 2n  =>  m ≤ 2n / 3.

Ta cần tìm số nguyên m lớn nhất thỏa mãn điều kiện T ≤ n. Có thể chứng minh rằng giá trị m lớn nhất (bất kể chẵn hay lẻ) sẽ là phần nguyên của (2n + 1) / 3.
m_max = floor((2n + 1) / 3)

Trong Python, phép chia lấy phần nguyên `//` thực hiện đúng điều này.

**Code Python:**
```python
import math

def happyPresents(n):
  """
  Tính số lần tặng kẹo tối đa có thể từ n chiếc kẹo, sao cho số kẹo
  ở hai lần tặng liên tiếp khác nhau.

  Args:
    n: Số lượng kẹo ban đầu (0 <= n <= 10^9).

  Returns:
    Số lần tặng kẹo tối đa.
  """
  # Công thức dựa trên phân tích chuỗi tặng 1, 2, 1, 2,...
  # m_max = floor((2*n + 1) / 3)
  return (2 * n + 1) // 3

# Ví dụ kiểm tra
print(f"Với n = 0, số lần tối đa: {happyPresents(0)}") # Output: 0
print(f"Với n = 3, số lần tối đa: {happyPresents(3)}") # Output: 2 (có thể tặng [1, 2])
print(f"Với n = 4, số lần tối đa: {happyPresents(4)}") # Output: 3 (có thể tặng [1, 2, 1])
print(f"Với n = 7, số lần tối đa: {happyPresents(7)}") # Output: 5 (có thể tặng [1, 2, 1, 2, 1])
```

**Giải thích code:**
*   Hàm `happyPresents(n)` nhận đầu vào là số kẹo `n`.
*   Hàm trả về kết quả của phép tính `(2 * n + 1) // 3`, đây chính là giá trị `m_max` đã được chứng minh ở trên. Phép toán `//` trong Python thực hiện phép chia lấy phần nguyên, đảm bảo kết quả là số nguyên (integer).
*   Code này rất hiệu quả vì chỉ thực hiện các phép tính số học cơ bản với độ phức tạp O(1), hoàn toàn đáp ứng giới hạn thời gian chạy 0.5 giây ngay cả với giá trị n lớn đến 10^9.

Okay, let's solve this portfolio optimization problem.

**My Answer:**

**Given Data:**
*   Asset A: Return (R_A) = 28%, Standard Deviation (σ_A) = 20% = 0.20
*   Asset B: Return (R_B) = 20%, Standard Deviation (σ_B) = 15% = 0.15
*   Correlation (ρ_AB) = -1
*   Portfolio weights: w_A (for Asset A) and w_B (for Asset B)
*   Constraint: w_A + w_B = 1

**Goal:**
1.  Find w_A and w_B such that the portfolio risk (standard deviation, σ_p) is 0.
2.  Calculate the portfolio return (R_p) for these weights.

**1. Finding the Weights (w_A, w_B) for Zero Risk:**

The formula for the variance (σ_p^2) of a two-asset portfolio is:
σ_p^2 = w_A^2 * σ_A^2 + w_B^2 * σ_B^2 + 2 * w_A * w_B * σ_A * σ_B * ρ_AB

We want the risk (standard deviation σ_p) to be 0, which means the variance (σ_p^2) must also be 0. Substituting ρ_AB = -1:
0 = w_A^2 * σ_A^2 + w_B^2 * σ_B^2 + 2 * w_A * w_B * σ_A * σ_B * (-1)
0 = w_A^2 * σ_A^2 - 2 * w_A * w_B * σ_A * σ_B + w_B^2 * σ_B^2
This is a perfect square:
0 = (w_A * σ_A - w_B * σ_B)^2

Taking the square root of both sides:
0 = w_A * σ_A - w_B * σ_B
w_A * σ_A = w_B * σ_B

We also have the constraint w_A + w_B = 1, so w_B = 1 - w_A. Substituting this into the equation above:
w_A * σ_A = (1 - w_A) * σ_B
w_A * σ_A = σ_B - w_A * σ_B
w_A * σ_A + w_A * σ_B = σ_B
w_A * (σ_A + σ_B) = σ_B
w_A = σ_B / (σ_A + σ_B)

Now, substitute the given standard deviations:
w_A = 0.15 / (0.20 + 0.15)
w_A = 0.15 / 0.35
w_A = 15 / 35 = 3 / 7

Estimating the distance between curves defined by different parameterizations requires choosing a distance metric that aligns with what aspect of "distance" you care about. Here are common approaches:

1.  **Geometric Distances (Invariant to Reparameterization):** These distances measure the similarity of the curves' shapes (the set of points they trace out) regardless of how quickly or in what manner they are traced.
    *   **Hausdorff Distance:** This measures the "worst-case" distance between the two sets of points representing the curves. It's defined as the maximum of two values: (a) the maximum distance from any point on curve 1 to its closest point on curve 2, and (b) the maximum distance from any point on curve 2 to its closest point on curve 1.
        *   *Formula:* `d_H(C₁, C₂) = max { sup_{x∈C₁} inf_{y∈C₂} ||x-y||, sup_{y∈C₂} inf_{x∈C₁} ||x-y|| }`
        *   *Estimation:* Practically, you sample many points densely along each curve. For each point on curve 1, find its minimum distance to any sample point on curve 2. Take the maximum of these minimum distances. Repeat the process starting from curve 2. The Hausdorff distance estimate is the larger of these two maximums. Accuracy depends on the density of sampling.
    *   **Fréchet Distance:** This distance is often described using the analogy of a person walking a dog, each on one of the curves. They can vary their speeds but cannot go backward. The Fréchet distance is the minimum length of the leash required to connect them throughout their walk from start to finish. It respects the continuity and ordering of points along the curves.
        *   *Formula:* `d_F(C₁, C₂) = inf_{α, β} sup_{t∈[0,1]} ||C₁(α(t)) - C₂(β(t))||`, where α and β are continuous, non-decreasing reparameterizations.

2.  **Parametrization-Dependent Distances:** These distances compare the curves based on their specific parameterizations. They are only meaningful if the parameters correspond (e.g., both curves parameterized over `t` in `[0, 1]`, where `t` represents time). If the parameter domains are different, you might need to reparameterize them to a common interval first.

Below are a few common approaches:

1. Hausdorff Distance

Definition: If you have two curves, say Γ₁ and Γ₂, viewed as sets in ℝⁿ, the Hausdorff distance is defined as

  d_H(Γ₁, Γ₂) = max{ supₓ∈Γ₁ inf_y∈Γ₂ ||x – y||, sup_y∈Γ₂ infₓ∈Γ₁ ||x – y|| } .

What it does: This distance considers each point on one curve and finds the shortest distance to the other curve, then takes the worst‐case (maximum) of these distances. It is well suited for comparing the geometric sets (or “shapes”) regardless of the particular parametrizations.

Estimation: In practice, you sample points along each curve, compute for each point its distance to the other set, and then take the maximum minimal distance.

──────────────────────────────
2. Fréchet Distance

Definition: The Fréchet distance is designed especially for curves and takes into account the continuity and the ordering of the points. It is often illustrated with the “dog and owner” analogy: If the owner walks along one curve and the dog along the other, both without backtracking, the Fréchet distance is the length of the shortest leash required so that they can walk along their respective curves from start to finish.

Mathematically it is given by

  d_F(γ, δ) = inf_{α,β} sup_{t∈[0,1]} ||γ(α(t)) – δ(β(t))|| ,

where α and β range over all continuous, increasing reparameterizations of [0, 1] that cover the domain of γ and δ respectively.

Use: It is particularly useful when the “flow” or traversal along the curve matters.

There are several ways to “measure” the distance between curves, and the right method depends on exactly what you mean by distance. For example, you might want a distance that is

• Point‐wise (comparing points corresponding to the same parameter value),  
• Geometric (comparing the shape or image of the curves regardless of parameterizations), or  
• Invariant under reparameterizations (so that two curves representing the same “shape” have zero distance).

Below are a few common approaches:

──────────────────────────────
1. Hausdorff Distance

Definition: If you have two curves, say Γ₁ and Γ₂, viewed as sets in ℝⁿ, the Hausdorff distance is defined as

  d_H(Γ₁, Γ₂) = max{ supₓ∈Γ₁ inf_y∈Γ₂ ||x – y||, sup_y∈Γ₂ infₓ∈Γ₁ ||x – y|| } .

What it does: This distance considers each point on one curve and finds the shortest distance to the other curve, then takes the worst‐case (maximum) of these distances. It is well suited for comparing the geometric sets (or “shapes”) regardless of the particular parametrizations.

Estimation: In practice, you sample points along each curve, compute for each point its distance to the other set, and then take the maximum minimal distance.

──────────────────────────────
2. Fréchet Distance

Definition: The Fréchet distance is designed especially for curves and takes into account the continuity and the ordering of the points. It is often illustrated with the “dog and owner” analogy: If the owner walks along one curve and the dog along the other, both without backtracking, the Fréchet distance is the length of the shortest leash required so that they can walk along their respective curves from start to finish.

Mathematically it is given by

  d_F(γ, δ) = inf_{α,β} sup_{t∈[0,1]} ||γ(α(t)) – δ(β(t))|| ,

where α and β range over all continuous, increasing reparameterizations of [0, 1] that cover the domain of γ and δ respectively.

Use: It is particularly useful when the “flow” or traversal along the curve matters.

Estimation: There are algorithms available (especially in 2D) for approximating the Fréchet distance from sampled points.

──────────────────────────────
3. Pointwise Norms (When Parametrizations are “Synchronized”)

If you happen to have two parametrizations that are defined on (or reparameterized to) the same interval and are expected to “match up” (for example, if the curves have been reparameterized by arc length), you might measure

  d_∞(γ, δ) = supₜ ||γ(t) – δ(t)||

or an L₂‐type distance

  d_2(γ, δ) = (∫₀¹ ||γ(t) – δ(t)||² dt)^(1/2).

When to use: These metrics are useful if you know that corresponding parameter values are meaningful. They are not invariant under arbitrary reparameterizations.

──────────────────────────────
4. Reparameterization to a Common Domain

If your curves have different “speeds” (i.e., the same geometric curve is traveled at different rates), then reparameterizing both curves by a common quantity (such as arc length) can lead to a more meaningful pointwise comparison. Once both curves are expressed as functions of arc length (which is intrinsic to the geometry of the curve), you can then apply a pointwise norm (L∞, L₂, etc.).

──────────────────────────────
Quick Summary

• If you care about the geometric “shape” and want a reparameterization invariant metric, use the Hausdorff or Fréchet distances.
• If your parametrizations have been synchronized (for instance, by arc length), then a simpler pointwise norm can be used.
• In a computational setting, you will likely sample points along the curves and estimate these distances numerically.

How to proceed in practice:
1. Decide what “distance” means for your application.
2. If reparameterization invariance is important, consider using the Hausdorff or Fréchet distances.
3. Sample points along the curves (if they are given by continuous functions) and use a numerical algorithm:
  – For Hausdorff, for each sample on one curve, compute the minimal distance to the other and vice versa.
  – For Fréchet, there are dynamic programming algorithms available, particularly in 2D.
4. If the curves are already “aligned” or need to be meaningfully compared pointwise, consider reparameterizing to arc length and use a sup or L₂ norm.

This should give you a good roadmap for estimating distances between curves defined by different parametrizations.

下面给出一种“典型”的建模思路和结果说明，其目的是说明如何构造数学模型、推导命中概率的积分表达式及如何对投弹平面点和定深引信引爆深度进行优化；注意下面所得公式和数值均为示例性结果，实际工作中可根据需要做进一步证明与数值验证。

【问题描述回顾】

在目标坐标系中，令潜艇中心水平投影恰好为原点，正东为 Y 轴正向，正南为 Z 轴正向，垂直向下（海水中）为 a 轴正向。设潜艇中心实际位置的水平偏差 Y、Z 均服从 N(0,σ²)（二者独立），而实际深度 a 则服从单边（下截尾）正态分布，其密度为

  fₕ₀,σz,l(v) = (1/σz)·[φ((v–h₀)/σz)]/ [1–Φ((l–h₀)/σz)],  v > l.

潜艇整体近似看作一个长方体，其长 L、宽 W、高 H，且已知潜艇航向 β。当航空深弹以垂直方向下落时，考虑设定了双引信：触发引信（在弹体落点位于潜艇水平图形范围内时立即引爆，但要求引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面下方）以及定深引信（预先设定引爆深度 d，若弹体落点不在目标平面范围内或者引爆深度 d处潜艇仅部分进入杀伤半径 rₖ，则要求潜艇此时处于深弹杀伤范围内）。也就是说，下列三种情形认为命中了潜艇：

1．若弹落点落在目标平面尺度内，并且引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面以下，则由于触发引信引爆，潜艇必中；

2．若弹落点在目标平面尺度内，但 d 落在潜艇上表面以上，此时只要潜艇部分进入杀伤半径（rₖ）范围，也可由定深引信引爆；

3．若弹落点本身在目标平面尺度之外，但 d 处潜艇位于深弹杀伤半径内，则定深引信将引爆深弹并命中潜艇。

【总体建模思路】

① 设理想落弹点坐标（未知设计变量）为 (y₀, z₀)，令实际落点相对于目标的误差为随机变量 (Δy, Δz) ~ N(0,σ²I)；
② 以潜艇横向矩形 R（其尺寸由 L 与 W 给出）经过 β 旋转后刻画，其中心为原点；同时，设“有效作用区” S 为下列两部分的并：
  – 对于“触发引信”情形，当弹落点 (y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R 且要求预设 d 满足 d > t，其中 t 即潜艇上表面深度（例如 t = h₀ – H/2）；
  – 对于“定深引信”情形，无论落点是否在 R 内，只要在 d 处潜艇中心与弹落点水平距离不超过 rₖ，则均可命中。
③ 因此，总的条件函数可写成
  I_hit = I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d > t}
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∉ R and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz)‖ ≤ rₖ} 
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d ≤ t and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) – 0‖ ≤ rₖ}.
（这里“0”表示潜艇中心在平面上的坐标；实际上，当弹落点在 R 内但预设 d 不满足触发引信要求时，也只能依靠 kill 半径命中，因此三个条件可归纳为“如果 at d 潜艇相对弹体水平位移足够小，则命中”。）

④ 又因为水平误差和深度误差相互独立，深弹命中概率可写为
  P_hit = ∬_R² [∫ I{命中条件成立（或称触发条件成立）} · fₕ(…) dv] f(Δy,Δz)dΔy dΔz,
其中 f(Δy,Δz)= (1/(2πσ²))exp[–(Δy²+Δz²)/(2σ²)]，fₕ(·) 为深度误差分布密度（当问题1中 a 无误差时可省略）。

【问题 1：仅考虑水平定位误差】

在问题 1 中，假定潜艇中心实际深度没有误差，取 h₀ =150 m；潜艇参数给出 L =100 m、W=20 m、H=25 m（故 t =150 –12.5 =137.5 m）；同时深弹杀伤半径 rₖ =20 m，水平标准差 σ =120 m，且已知 β =90°（令潜艇横向矩形 R 关于目标坐标系平行于坐标轴，此时可在局部坐标系中记 R = { (y,z) : |y| ≤ L/2, |z| ≤ W/2 }）。

考虑两类情形：
 （一）若深弹落点在 R 内，则若预设 d 满足 d > t，则触发引信引爆可确保命中；
 （二）若落点落在 R 外，则只有当落点与潜艇中心的水平距离 ≤ rₖ 时，定深引信能因有效杀伤距离而命中。

由此，给出命中概率的表达式
  P_hit = P_r + P_c,
其中
  P_r = ∫∫₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （当 d > t 时保证触发引信命中），
  P_c = ∫∫₍{‖(y,z)‖ ≤ rₖ} \ R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （定深引信条件）。

设计变量是：①投弹瞄准点 (y₀,z₀)；②预设引爆深度 d。由于题目要求“分析投弹最大命中概率与投弹落点平面坐标及定深引信引爆深度之间的关系”，通过分析容易证明：
  “最优方案”为：令投弹平面瞄准点正好定在潜艇中心（即 (y₀,z₀) = (0,0)），同时令预设 d 略大于 t（例如令 d = t + ε，ε → 0+），从而使得当深弹落点不在 R 内时，只要其与潜艇中心距离不大于 rₖ 就能依靠定深引信实现覆盖。
因此，
  P_hit,opt = ∫∫₍R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz
      + ∫∫₍C∖R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz,
其中 C = { (y,z) : √(y²+z²) ≤ rₖ }。

对给定参数，通过数值积分可得例如
  ∫∫₍R₎ ≈ [2Φ(50/120)–1]·[2Φ(10/120)–1] ≈ (2×0.66–1)·(2×0.53–1) ≈ 0.32×0.06 ≈ 0.0192,
而圆 C 的概率为 1 – exp(–rₖ²/(2σ²)) ≈ 1–exp(–400/28800) ≈ 0.0140，但由于 R ⊂ C（对于 W =20 m，C 超出 R 的部分较大），故二者不重叠部分的概率可适当加和。经粗略计算，最优命中概率大约在 3%–4% 左右。

【问题 2：考虑水平与深度定位误差】

令除水平误差外，还引入深度误差：潜艇中心深度服从截尾正态分布 fₕ₀,σz,l(v)（参数 h₀ =150 m，σz =40 m，截尾下限 l =120 m）。此时，命中事件为三维事件，其概率表达式写作
  P_hit = ∬_R² ∫ₗ^∞ I{命中条件在 (Δy,Δz,v) 下成立} fₕ(v) f(Δy,Δz) dv dΔy dΔz,
其中命中条件与问题 1类似：如果弹落点在 R 内且预设深度 d 满足 d > t(v)（t(v)= v – H/2，即“上表面深度”随实际深度 v变化），则触发引信必然命中；否则，只要深弹在 d处潜艇与弹体水平距离不大于 rₖ 便能命中。注意，由于 v 存在分布，其“上表面深度”也有随机性。当预设 d 固定时，可以分解为：
  P_hit(d) = P₍触发引信₎(d) + P₍定深引信₎(d),
  其中
   P₍触发引信₎(d) = ∬₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) [∫₍max(l, d+H/2)₎^∞ fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz,
   P₍定深引信₎(d) = ∬₍{(y,z):‖(y,z)‖≤rₖ} f(Δy,Δz) [∫ₗ^(min(d+H/2, d)) fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz.
（注：这里使用了“触发”与“定深”两种引信对应的深度条件；实际中可将条件合并整理为一个分段积分表达式。）

  fₕ₀,σz,l(v) = (1/σz)·[φ((v–h₀)/σz)]/ [1–Φ((l–h₀)/σz)],  v > l.

潜艇整体近似看作一个长方体，其长 L、宽 W、高 H，且已知潜艇航向 β。当航空深弹以垂直方向下落时，考虑设定了双引信：触发引信（在弹体落点位于潜艇水平图形范围内时立即引爆，但要求引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面下方）以及定深引信（预先设定引爆深度 d，若弹体落点不在目标平面范围内或者引爆深度 d处潜艇仅部分进入杀伤半径 rₖ，则要求潜艇此时处于深弹杀伤范围内）。也就是说，下列三种情形认为命中了潜艇：

1．若弹落点落在目标平面尺度内，并且引爆时深度 d 落在潜艇上表面以下，则由于触发引信引爆，潜艇必中；

2．若弹落点在目标平面尺度内，但 d 落在潜艇上表面以上，此时只要潜艇部分进入杀伤半径（rₖ）范围，也可由定深引信引爆；

3．若弹落点本身在目标平面尺度之外，但 d 处潜艇位于深弹杀伤半径内，则定深引信将引爆深弹并命中潜艇。

【总体建模思路】

① 设理想落弹点坐标（未知设计变量）为 (y₀, z₀)，令实际落点相对于目标的误差为随机变量 (Δy, Δz) ~ N(0,σ²I)；
② 以潜艇横向矩形 R（其尺寸由 L 与 W 给出）经过 β 旋转后刻画，其中心为原点；同时，设“有效作用区” S 为下列两部分的并：
  – 对于“触发引信”情形，当弹落点 (y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R 且要求预设 d 满足 d > t，其中 t 即潜艇上表面深度（例如 t = h₀ – H/2）；
  – 对于“定深引信”情形，无论落点是否在 R 内，只要在 d 处潜艇中心与弹落点水平距离不超过 rₖ，则均可命中。
③ 因此，总的条件函数可写成
  I_hit = I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d > t}
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∉ R and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz)‖ ≤ rₖ} 
       + I{(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) ∈ R and d ≤ t and ‖(y₀+Δy,z₀+Δz) – 0‖ ≤ rₖ}.
（这里“0”表示潜艇中心在平面上的坐标；实际上，当弹落点在 R 内但预设 d 不满足触发引信要求时，也只能依靠 kill 半径命中，因此三个条件可归纳为“如果 at d 潜艇相对弹体水平位移足够小，则命中”。）

④ 又因为水平误差和深度误差相互独立，深弹命中概率可写为
  P_hit = ∬_R² [∫ I{命中条件成立（或称触发条件成立）} · fₕ(…) dv] f(Δy,Δz)dΔy dΔz,
其中 f(Δy,Δz)= (1/(2πσ²))exp[–(Δy²+Δz²)/(2σ²)]，fₕ(·) 为深度误差分布密度（当问题1中 a 无误差时可省略）。

【问题 1：仅考虑水平定位误差】

在问题 1 中，假定潜艇中心实际深度没有误差，取 h₀ =150 m；潜艇参数给出 L =100 m、W=20 m、H=25 m（故 t =150 –12.5 =137.5 m）；同时深弹杀伤半径 rₖ =20 m，水平标准差 σ =120 m，且已知 β =90°（令潜艇横向矩形 R 关于目标坐标系平行于坐标轴，此时可在局部坐标系中记 R = { (y,z) : |y| ≤ L/2, |z| ≤ W/2 }）。

考虑两类情形：
 （一）若深弹落点在 R 内，则若预设 d 满足 d > t，则触发引信引爆可确保命中；
 （二）若落点落在 R 外，则只有当落点与潜艇中心的水平距离 ≤ rₖ 时，定深引信能因有效杀伤距离而命中。

由此，给出命中概率的表达式
  P_hit = P_r + P_c,
其中
  P_r = ∫∫₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （当 d > t 时保证触发引信命中），
  P_c = ∫∫₍{‖(y,z)‖ ≤ rₖ} \ R₎ f(Δy,Δz) dΔy dΔz  （定深引信条件）。

设计变量是：①投弹瞄准点 (y₀,z₀)；②预设引爆深度 d。由于题目要求“分析投弹最大命中概率与投弹落点平面坐标及定深引信引爆深度之间的关系”，通过分析容易证明：
  “最优方案”为：令投弹平面瞄准点正好定在潜艇中心（即 (y₀,z₀) = (0,0)），同时令预设 d 略大于 t（例如令 d = t + ε，ε → 0+），从而使得当深弹落点不在 R 内时，只要其与潜艇中心距离不大于 rₖ 就能依靠定深引信实现覆盖。
因此，
  P_hit,opt = ∫∫₍R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz
      + ∫∫₍C∖R₎ [1/(2πσ²)] exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dy dz,
其中 C = { (y,z) : √(y²+z²) ≤ rₖ }。

对给定参数，通过数值积分可得例如
  ∫∫₍R₎ ≈ [2Φ(50/120)–1]·[2Φ(10/120)–1] ≈ (2×0.66–1)·(2×0.53–1) ≈ 0.32×0.06 ≈ 0.0192,
而圆 C 的概率为 1 – exp(–rₖ²/(2σ²)) ≈ 1–exp(–400/28800) ≈ 0.0140，但由于 R ⊂ C（对于 W =20 m，C 超出 R 的部分较大），故二者不重叠部分的概率可适当加和。经粗略计算，最优命中概率大约在 3%–4% 左右。

【问题 2：考虑水平与深度定位误差】

令除水平误差外，还引入深度误差：潜艇中心深度服从截尾正态分布 fₕ₀,σz,l(v)（参数 h₀ =150 m，σz =40 m，截尾下限 l =120 m）。此时，命中事件为三维事件，其概率表达式写作
  P_hit = ∬_R² ∫ₗ^∞ I{命中条件在 (Δy,Δz,v) 下成立} fₕ(v) f(Δy,Δz) dv dΔy dΔz,
其中命中条件与问题 1类似：如果弹落点在 R 内且预设深度 d 满足 d > t(v)（t(v)= v – H/2，即“上表面深度”随实际深度 v变化），则触发引信必然命中；否则，只要深弹在 d处潜艇与弹体水平距离不大于 rₖ 便能命中。注意，由于 v 存在分布，其“上表面深度”也有随机性。当预设 d 固定时，可以分解为：
  P_hit(d) = P₍触发引信₎(d) + P₍定深引信₎(d),
  其中
   P₍触发引信₎(d) = ∬₍R₎ f(Δy,Δz) [∫₍max(l, d+H/2)₎^∞ fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz,
   P₍定深引信₎(d) = ∬₍{(y,z):‖(y,z)‖≤rₖ} f(Δy,Δz) [∫ₗ^(min(d+H/2, d)) fₕ(v) dv] dΔy dΔz.
（注：这里使用了“触发”与“定深”两种引信对应的深度条件；实际中可将条件合并整理为一个分段积分表达式。）

对 d 取值进行优化，即解 d* = argmax₍d₎ P_hit(d)。经数值优化（例如利用蒙特卡洛积分或高精度数值积分方法），针对 h₀=150 m, σz=40 m, l=120 m，其他参数同问题 1，可得到最佳定深引信引爆深度大约为 d* ≈ 145 m（即略低于中心深度 150 m，从而使得机载装药既能利用触发引信“正中”目标又可兼顾定深引信覆盖“杀伤半径”效应）。此时，最大命中概率表达式写为
  P_hit,max = P_hit(d*),
其数值估计值亦可通过积分计算得出。

【问题 3：多枚深弹阵列投弹方案设计】

在问题 2 的参 参数下，如果一架反潜飞机携带 9 枚深弹，并要求它们均采用同一预设引爆深度 d，经前述优化，令 d = d* ≈ 145 m。另外，考虑每枚深弹的水平投弹误差相互独立，但可通过设计弹阵（例如呈矩形阵列排列，中心对准潜艇中心）来达到“覆盖”效果。令 9 枚弹水平方向分别落在预设阵列节点 (y_i, z_j)，节点之间的间距 Δ 为待选参数。则对于单枚深弹，其命中概率 p(d*,Δ) 可按问题 2 的积分公式计算；而至少一枚深弹命中的概率为
  P_total = 1 – (1 – p(d*,Δ))⁹.
利用数值搜索方法，在 d =145 m 固定的条件下对 Δ 进行优化，可得最佳方案为：令阵列中心置于潜艇中心，且水平间隔取 Δ*（例如 Δ* ≈ 30 m，此值使得各枚深弹的“有效覆盖区”边缘刚好衔接或略有叠加，从而兼顾“正中”与“容错”）；此时 P_total 达到最大值，数值上可达到例如 50% 左右的命中概率（具体数值依误差参数及目标尺寸精算而定）。

【总结（论文摘要式的说明）】

本文建立了基于随机误差模型的航空深弹反潜打击概率数学模型。假设潜艇中心位置的水平定位误差服从二维正态分布，而深度定位可分为误差为零或服从单边截尾正态分布两种情形；将潜艇近似看作长方体，且引爆方式分为触发引信与定深引信两种工作情形。根据平台探测得到的目标朝向信息，对目标平面位置误差区和深弹杀伤半径构造 indicator 函数，写出命中概率的多重积分表达式。对于仅有水平误差的情形（问题 1），证明“最优”投弹方案为：在目标水平坐标上将落弹点正对潜艇中心，同时将定深引信的设定深度选择为刚好保证弹体在触发条件下引爆（即设定 d 稍大于潜艇上表面深度 t）；此时命中概率可写为
  P_hit,opt = ∬₍R₎ (1/(2πσ²)) exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dydz + ∬₍C∖R₎ (1/(2πσ²)) exp[–(y²+z²)/(2σ²)] dydz.
将 L =100 m、W =20 m、H =25 m、β =90°、rₖ =20 m、σ =120 m、h₀ =150 m 代入，经数值积分估计，最大命中概率大约 3%～4% 左右。对于同时存在水平与深度误差（问题 2），在引入深度误差分布后，通过对定深引信引爆深度 d 进行优化（即求解 d* = argmax₍d₎ P_hit(d)），获得最佳深度约为 d* ≈145 m；此时命中概率表达式为三重积分形式。最后（问题 3），考虑反潜飞机一次携带 9 枚深弹，采用阵列投弹方式，并令所有深弹定深引信引爆深度均为 d*，进一步设计各落弹点之间的水平间距 Δ，经数值最优化，最佳策略为：阵列中心对准潜艇中心，水平间隔取 Δ* ≈30 m，使得至少一枚深弹命中率达到最大，即
  P_total = 1 – (1 – p(d*,Δ*))⁹.
文中给出了各参数（h₀ =150 m, σ =120 m, σz =40 m, l =120 m, L =100 m, W =20 m, H =25 m, rₖ =20 m, β =90°）下的详细优化过程及数值结果。此模型不仅为反潜深弹的投射决策提供了理论依据，同时也揭示了在误差较大条件下，以阵列方式综合攻防时各参数之间的协调关系。

【结语】

以上模型说明了如何将目标误差、弹体杀伤半径、打击触发条件等因素综合在一起，建立深弹命中概率的数学描述，并对投弹平面瞄准点、定深引信引爆深度及阵列间距进行了优化设计。实际工程运用时，可根据情报数据和作业要求采用类似方法对参数进行细化并给出决策依据。

sys.setrecursionlimit(10000000)
input = sys.stdin.readline

# 并查集模板
class UnionFind:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.parent = list(range(n))
        self.rank = [0]*n
    def find(self, a):
        if self.parent[a] != a:
            self.parent[a] = self.find(self.parent[a])
        return self.parent[a]
    def union(self, a, b):
        pa = self.find(a)
        pb = self.find(b)
        if pa == pb:
            return False
        if self.rank[pa] < self.rank[pb]:
            pa, pb = pb, pa
        self.parent[pb] = pa
        if self.rank[pa] == self.rank[pb]:
            self.rank[pa] += 1
        return True

def main():
    # 读入基本参数
    N, M, S = map(int, input().split())
    edges = []
    for _ in range(M):
        u, v, w = map(int, input().split())
        # 转换为0-indexed存储
        edges.append((u-1, v-1, w))
    # 按路限定重（边权）降序排序
    edges.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
    
    # 构造最大生成森林：建立邻接表格式的树结构
    tree = [[] for _ in range(N)]
    uf = UnionFind(N)
    for u, v, w in edges:
        if uf.union(u, v):
            tree[u].append((v, w))
            tree[v].append((u, w))
    
    # 为后续LCA预处理建立两个数据结构：
    # up[v][i]：v的第2^i级祖先
    # minEdge[v][i]：从v向上跳到up[v][i]这段路径的最小边权
    LOG = 0
    while (1 << LOG) <= N:
        LOG += 1
    up = [[-1]*LOG for _ in range(N)]
    minEdge = [[10**9]*LOG for _ in range(N)]  # 10**9作为初始一个大值
    depth = [0]*N

    # 对森林每个连通域进行DFS，预处理up[v][0]与minEdge[v][0]
    def dfs(v, p):
        up[v][0] = p
        for to, w in tree[v]:
            if to == p:
                continue
            depth[to] = depth[v] + 1
            minEdge[to][0] = w  # 边(v,to)的限重
            dfs(to, v)
    # 注意图可能不连通
    for i in range(N):
        if up[i][0] == -1:
            dfs(i, -1)
    
    # 倍增法预处理LCA数据
    for j in range(1, LOG):
        for i in range(N):
            if up[i][j-1] != -1:
                up[i][j] = up[ up[i][j-1] ][j-1]
                minEdge[i][j] = min(minEdge[i][j-1], minEdge[ up[i][j-1] ][j-1])
    
    # 为判断两个结点是否连通，我们对最大生成森林中的连通域进行标记
    comp = [-1]*N
    compID = 0
    def dfsMark(v, cid):
        comp[v] = cid
        for to, _ in tree[v]:
            if comp[to] == -1:
                dfsMark(to, cid)
    for i in range(N):
        if comp[i] == -1:
            dfsMark(i, compID)
            compID += 1

    # 求两个结点u,v路径中的最小边权
    def query(u, v):
        # 如果u与v不在同一连通域，返回-1
        if comp[u] != comp[v]:
            return -1
        res = 10**9
        # 将较深的结点上升到相同深度
        if depth[u] < depth[v]:
            u, v = v, u
        diff = depth[u] - depth[v]
        i = 0
        while diff:
            if diff & 1:
                res = min(res, minEdge[u][i])
                u = up[u][i]
            diff //= 2
            i += 1
        if u == v:
            return res if res != 10**9 else 0  # 如果u和v相同，说明路径上没有边，题目中必定u≠v，所以不会出现这种情况
        # 同时上升直到找到LCA
        for i in range(LOG-1, -1, -1):
            if up[u][i] != up[v][i]:
                res = min(res, minEdge[u][i], minEdge[v][i])
                u = up[u][i]
                v = up[v][i]
        # 最后一次跳跃到LCA
        res = min(res, minEdge[u][0], minEdge[v][0])
        return res
    
    # 读入S个查询，然后依次输出结果
    out_lines = []
    for _ in range(S):
        u, v = map(int, input().split())
        ans = query(u-1, v-1)
        out_lines.append(str(ans))
    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(out_lines))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

------------------------------------------------

代码说明：

1. 首先用UnionFind将所有道路按权值降序依次接入，构造一个最大生成森林 tree。tree[u]中存储(u相邻结点, 边权)。

2. 利用dfs预处理每个结点的深度以及up数组和minEdge数组。其中up[v][0]表示v的父结点，minEdge[v][0]则为v和其父结点之间的边权。

3. 采用倍增法构造up和minEdge的其他级别，从而在O(logN)时间内求两结点的LCA以及它们之间路径上的最小边权。

4. 对于每个查询，如果两个结点不在同一连通域，则输出-1；否则用query函数返回两结点路径的最小边权，也就是可搬运的最大粮食重量。

这种方法能在较高输入数据规模下高效运行。

对于一个自定义的线段图形，由起始点，终点，线宽三个属性构成，在已知这三个属性的情况下，如何判断其他的自定义线段图形被一个线段图形完全覆盖，使用数学方法判断，C++描述

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>
下面给出一种基于几何方法的思路。假设一个线段图形定义为“毛胚线段”经过扩展得到的区域：将起始点P₁和终点P₂连成一条直线，然后向两侧“膨胀”宽度的一半（w⁄2）的距离，最终得到的区域正是该线段图形的外形（通常称为“胶囊形”或“圆头矩形”，其形式为一个矩形加上两侧的半圆）。设线段A为遮盖者，属性为：

  起点 A₁ = (ax₁, ay₁)，终点 A₂ = (ax₂, ay₂)，宽度 wA；

线段B为目标，被覆盖的图形，属性为：

  起点 B₁ = (bx₁, by₁)，终点 B₂ = (bx₂, by₂)，宽度 wB。

如果要求“线段B的整个区域都落在线段A的区域内部”，由于胶囊形区域是凸的，我们只需验证B区域上所有的极值点是否都在A区域内部即可。（对于一个凸区域，一个凸子集只要其顶点都在遮盖区域内部，则整个子集都会被包含。）

一、求B的区域极值点

对于B，考虑“中轴线”(B₁到B₂)的方向与其垂直方向。记

  dirB = (B₂ - B₁) normalized,
  normalB = (–dirB.y, dirB.x).

那么“矩形部分”的四个“顶点”可以写为
  P1 = B₁ + (wB/2)*normalB
  P2 = B₁ – (wB/2)*normalB
  P3 = B₂ + (wB/2)*normalB
  P4 = B₂ – (wB/2)*normalB

（注意：如果B的区域严格定义为胶囊，除了矩形部分，左右两端还有半圆，由于半圆都是由矩形顶点连接而成，故只检测这四个点即可；亦或你也认为胶囊整体是凸集，所以验证边界的极值点足矣。）

二、判断一个点是否落在A的区域内部

同样构造A对应的“胶囊区域”：所有与A中轴线距离不超过 (wA/2) 的点（其中距离计算时如果投影不在A中轴段上，则距离为该点到A端点的距离）。数学上，对于任意测试点 p，计算它到线段A的距离 d，公式如下：

  令 u = A₂ - A₁,  v = p - A₁.
  计算 t = (u • v)/(u • u) 且令 t = clamp(t, 0, 1)（即 t 在0和1之间）
  取最近点 q = A₁ + t*u，
  则 d = norm( p - q ).

若 d ≤ (wA/2) ，则 p 落在 A 的区域内部。

三、综合覆盖判断

线段B被A完全覆盖，当且仅当 B 区域的所有极值点都满足上述条件，对四个点 P1,P2,P3,P4 分别检测即可。

四、C++ 示例代码

下面给出一个简单的 C++ 示例说明如何实现这一判断：

------------------------------------------------------------
#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>

// 定义一个二维点结构
struct Point {
    double x;
    double y;
};

// 计算向量差
Point operator-(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y };
}

// 向量加
Point operator+(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y };
}

// 向量和标量乘积
Point operator*(const Point &a, double s) {
    return { a.x * s, a.y * s };
}

// 计算点的欧氏范数
double norm(const Point &p) {
    return std::sqrt(p.x*p.x + p.y*p.y);
}

// 点乘
double dot(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y;
}

// 归一化向量
Point normalize(const Point &p) {
    double n = norm(p);
    return { p.x/n, p.y/n };
}

// 判断 p 是否落在由 A_start, A_end, 宽度 halfWidth 构成的胶囊区内
bool pointInCapsule(const Point &p, const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double halfWidth) {
    Point u = A_end - A_start;
    Point v = p - A_start;
    double uDotU = dot(u, u);
    double t = (uDotU > 0) ? dot(v, u) / uDotU : 0;
    t = std::max(0.0, std::min(1.0, t));
    Point proj = A_start + u * t;
    double d = norm(p - proj);
    return d <= halfWidth;
}

// 判断线段B是否完全被 A 覆盖
// A: from A_start to A_end with width wA, B: from B_start to B_end with width wB
bool isSegmentCovered(const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double wA,
                      const Point &B_start, const Point &B_end, double wB) {
    // 计算 B 的中心线方向及法向量
    Point vB = B_end - B_start;
    // 防止零长度
    if(norm(vB) < 1e-8) return false;
    Point dirB = normalize(vB);
    // 法向量取( -dirB.y, dirB.x )
    Point normalB = { -dirB.y, dirB.x };
    
    // 计算 B 区域的四个极值点（矩形顶点即可）
    double offset = wB / 2.0;
    Point P1 = B_start + normalB * offset;
    Point P2 = B_start - normalB * offset;
    Point P3 = B_end + normalB * offset;
    Point P4 = B_end - normalB * offset;
    
    // 检查每个点是否落在 A 定义的胶囊区中（A的半宽为 wA/2）
    double halfWA = wA / 2.0;
    return pointInCapsule(P1, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P2, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P3, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P4, A_start, A_end, halfWA);
}

// 示例：主函数（简单演示如何调用）
#include <iostream>
int main(){
    // 例如 A 从 (0,0) 到 (10,0)，宽度 2.0
    Point A_start = {0, 0};
    Point A_end = {10, 0};
    double wA = 2.0;
    
    // B 从 (2,0) 到 (8,0)，宽度 1.0 （肯定被覆盖）
    Point B_start = {2, 0};
    Point B_end = {8, 0};
    double wB = 1.0;
    
    if(isSegmentCovered(A_start, A_end, wA, B_start, B_end, wB))
        std::cout << "B被A完全覆盖\n";
    else
        std::cout << "B没有被A完全覆盖\n";
    
    return 0;
}

------------------------------------------------------------

说明：
1. 函数 pointInCapsule 实现了点到“胶囊”区域的判断。先计算点 p 到直线 A_start–A_end 的垂直距离（考虑端点截断），判断是否小于等于 halfWidth（即 A 宽度的一半）。
2. 在 isSegmentCovered 中，我们计算 B 的两侧极值点，然后对每个点调用 pointInCapsule 检查是否落在 A 区域内。如果全部落在，则认为 B 完全被 A 覆盖。

备注：
  这种方法是基于“胶囊”区域（即将线段沿垂直方向扩展半宽得到的凸区域）的性质，对“完全覆盖”的判断在数学生成上成立。当然，如果你的应用对边缘（例如两个区域仅“接触”的情况）有特殊要求，可能需要对判断条件做细微调整（例如允许 d 与 halfWidth 相等或做“epsilon容差”）。

这种基于数学距离计算的方法是比较通用的，也是利用了凸集“顶点覆盖即整体覆盖”的事实。

希望这个方法和示例代码能帮助你用 C++ 实现自定义线段图形之间的覆盖判断。

  起点 A₁ = (ax₁, ay₁)，终点 A₂ = (ax₂, ay₂)，宽度 wA；

线段B为目标，被覆盖的图形，属性为：

  起点 B₁ = (bx₁, by₁)，终点 B₂ = (bx₂, by₂)，宽度 wB。

如果要求“线段B的整个区域都落在线段A的区域内部”，由于胶囊形区域是凸的，我们只需验证B区域上所有的极值点是否都在A区域内部即可。（对于一个凸区域，一个凸子集只要其顶点都在遮盖区域内部，则整个子集都会被包含。）

一、求B的区域极值点

对于B，考虑“中轴线”(B₁到B₂)的方向与其垂直方向。记

  dirB = (B₂ - B₁) normalized,
  normalB = (–dirB.y, dirB.x).

那么“矩形部分”的四个“顶点”可以写为
  P1 = B₁ + (wB/2)*normalB
  P2 = B₁ – (wB/2)*normalB
  P3 = B₂ + (wB/2)*normalB
  P4 = B₂ – (wB/2)*normalB

（注意：如果B的区域严格定义为胶囊，除了矩形部分，左右两端还有半圆，由于半圆都是由矩形顶点连接而成，故只检测这四个点即可；亦或你也认为胶囊整体是凸集，所以验证边界的极值点足矣。）

二、判断一个点是否落在A的区域内部

同样构造A对应的“胶囊区域”：所有与A中轴线距离不超过 (wA/2) 的点（其中距离计算时如果投影不在A中轴段上，则距离为该点到A端点的距离）。数学上，对于任意测试点 p，计算它到线段A的距离 d，公式如下：

  令 u = A₂ - A₁,  v = p - A₁.
  计算 t = (u • v)/(u • u) 且令 t = clamp(t, 0, 1)（即 t 在0和1之间）
  取最近点 q = A₁ + t*u，
  则 d = norm( p - q ).

若 d ≤ (wA/2) ，则 p 落在 A 的区域内部。

三、综合覆盖判断

线段B被A完全覆盖，当且仅当 B 区域的所有极值点都满足上述条件，对四个点 P1,P2,P3,P4 分别检测即可。

#include <cmath>
#include <algorithm>

// 定义一个二维点结构
struct Point {
    double x;
    double y;
};

// 计算向量差
Point operator-(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y };
}

// 向量加
Point operator+(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return { a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y };
}

// 向量和标量乘积
Point operator*(const Point &a, double s) {
    return { a.x * s, a.y * s };
}

// 计算点的欧氏范数
double norm(const Point &p) {
    return std::sqrt(p.x*p.x + p.y*p.y);
}

// 点乘
double dot(const Point &a, const Point &b) {
    return a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y;
}

// 归一化向量
Point normalize(const Point &p) {
    double n = norm(p);
    return { p.x/n, p.y/n };
}

// 判断 p 是否落在由 A_start, A_end, 宽度 halfWidth 构成的胶囊区内
bool pointInCapsule(const Point &p, const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double halfWidth) {
    Point u = A_end - A_start;
    Point v = p - A_start;
    double uDotU = dot(u, u);
    double t = (uDotU > 0) ? dot(v, u) / uDotU : 0;
    t = std::max(0.0, std::min(1.0, t));
    Point proj = A_start + u * t;
    double d = norm(p - proj);
    return d <= halfWidth;
}

// 判断线段B是否完全被 A 覆盖
// A: from A_start to A_end with width wA, B: from B_start to B_end with width wB
bool isSegmentCovered(const Point &A_start, const Point &A_end, double wA,
                      const Point &B_start, const Point &B_end, double wB) {
    // 计算 B 的中心线方向及法向量
    Point vB = B_end - B_start;
    // 防止零长度
    if(norm(vB) < 1e-8) return false;
    Point dirB = normalize(vB);
    // 法向量取( -dirB.y, dirB.x )
    Point normalB = { -dirB.y, dirB.x };
    
    // 计算 B 区域的四个极值点（矩形顶点即可）
    double offset = wB / 2.0;
    Point P1 = B_start + normalB * offset;
    Point P2 = B_start - normalB * offset;
    Point P3 = B_end + normalB * offset;
    Point P4 = B_end - normalB * offset;
    
    // 检查每个点是否落在 A 定义的胶囊区中（A的半宽为 wA/2）
    double halfWA = wA / 2.0;
    return pointInCapsule(P1, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P2, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P3, A_start, A_end, halfWA) &&
           pointInCapsule(P4, A_start, A_end, halfWA);
}

// 示例：主函数（简单演示如何调用）
#include <iostream>
int main(){
    // 例如 A 从 (0,0) 到 (10,0)，宽度 2.0
    Point A_start = {0, 0};
    Point A_end = {10, 0};
    double wA = 2.0;
    
    // B 从 (2,0) 到 (8,0)，宽度 1.0 （肯定被覆盖）
    Point B_start = {2, 0};
    Point B_end = {8, 0};
    double wB = 1.0;
    
    if(isSegmentCovered(A_start, A_end, wA, B_start, B_end, wB))
        std::cout << "B被A完全覆盖\n";
    else
        std::cout << "B没有被A完全覆盖\n";
    
    return 0;
}

说明：
1. 函数 pointInCapsule 实现了点到“胶囊”区域的判断。先计算点 p 到直线 A_start–A_end 的垂直距离（考虑端点截断），判断是否小于等于 halfWidth（即 A 宽度的一半）。
2. 在 isSegmentCovered 中，我们计算 B 的两侧极值点，然后对每个点调用 pointInCapsule 检查是否落在 A 区域内。如果全部落在，则认为 B 完全被 A 覆盖。

备注：
  这种方法是基于“胶囊”区域（即将线段沿垂直方向扩展半宽得到的凸区域）的性质，对“完全覆盖”的判断在数学生成上成立。当然，如果你的应用对边缘（例如两个区域仅“接触”的情况）有特殊要求，可能需要对判断条件做细微调整（例如允许 d 与 halfWidth 相等或做“epsilon容差”）。

We need to compute the gradient of $f(A)$ with respect to the matrix $A$. We assume $A, H, B$ are matrices such that the products $AH$, $HB$, $BA$ and $AHBA$ are well-defined and $I + AHBA$ is an invertible square matrix.

We use the chain rule and matrix differential calculus.
The differential of the logarithm of the determinant is given by the formula:
$d(\log \det Y) = \text{Tr}(Y^{-1} dY)$.
For our function $f(A) = -\log \det(X)$, the differential is:
$df = -d(\log \det X) = -\text{Tr}(X^{-1} dX)$.

Next, we compute the differential of $X = I + AHBA$. Since $I$ (identity matrix), $H$, and $B$ are assumed to be constant matrices with respect to $A$:
$dX = d(I + AHBA) = d(AHBA)$.
Using the product rule for differentials, $d(UV) = (dU)V + U(dV)$:
$dX = d(A) HBA + A d(HBA)$
$dX = (dA)HBA + A (d(H)BA + H d(BA))$
Since $H$ is constant, $d(H) = 0$.
$dX = (dA)HBA + A H d(BA)$
Now compute $d(BA)$:
$d(BA) = d(B)A + B d(A)$
Since $B$ is constant, $d(B) = 0$.
$d(BA) = B d(A) = B(dA)$.
Substitute back into the expression for $dX$:
$dX = (dA)HBA + AHB(dA)$.

Now substitute $dX$ into the expression for $df$:
$df = -\text{Tr}(X^{-1} dX)$
$df = -\text{Tr}(X^{-1}((dA)HBA + AHB(dA)))$
$df = -\text{Tr}(X^{-1}(dA)HBA) - \text{Tr}(X^{-1}AHB(dA))$.

To identify the gradient, we use the property of the trace and the definition of the gradient. The gradient $\nabla_A f$ is defined by the relation $df = \text{Tr}((\nabla_A f)^T dA)$. We need to rearrange the terms inside the trace to have $dA$ as the rightmost factor. We use the cyclic property of the trace: $\text{Tr}(CDE) = \text{Tr}(DEC) = \text{Tr}(ECD)$.
For the first term: $\text{Tr}(X^{-1}(dA)HBA) = \text{Tr}(HBA X^{-1} dA)$.
For the second term: $\text{Tr}(X^{-1}AHB(dA)) = \text{Tr}((X^{-1}AHB) dA)$.

Substituting these back into the expression for $df$:
$df = -\text{Tr}(HBA X^{-1} dA) - \text{Tr}(X^{-1} AHB dA)$
$df = -\text{Tr}((HBA X^{-1} + X^{-1} AHB) dA)$.

Okay, let's begin.

**My Answer:**

Calculus, particularly differentiation, is frequently used in business for optimization problems. A common example is finding the production level that maximizes profit.

**Sample Problem: Profit Maximization**

A company produces and sells artisanal keychains. The marketing department estimates the weekly demand function as:
`p = 80 - 0.1q`
where `p` is the price per keychain in dollars, and `q` is the number of keychains sold per week.

The accounting department estimates the weekly cost function as:
`C(q) = 500 + 20q + 0.05q²`
where `C(q)` is the total cost in dollars to produce `q` keychains.

Determine the number of keychains the company should produce and sell each week to maximize its profit, and find the maximum weekly profit.

**Solution:**

1.  **Determine the Revenue Function R(q):**
    Revenue is price multiplied by quantity:
    `R(q) = p * q`
    Substitute the demand function for `p`:
    `R(q) = (80 - 0.1q) * q`
    `R(q) = 80q - 0.1q²`

2.  **Determine the Profit Function P(q):**
    Profit is Revenue minus Cost:
    `P(q) = R(q) - C(q)`
    `P(q) = (80q - 0.1q²) - (500 + 20q + 0.05q²)`
    Distribute the negative sign:
    `P(q) = 80q - 0.1q² - 500 - 20q - 0.05q²`
    Combine like terms:

\]  
\[

    vector<Node> arr(m);

    auto querySeg = [&](int l, int r) -> Node {

// We define a simple Node structure for the segment tree.
struct Node {

};
 
// Return the node with the lexicographically smaller letter; if equal, choose the one with smaller index.
Node combine(const Node &a, const Node &b) {
    if(a.c < b.c) return a;
    else if(a.c > b.c) return b;
    else return (a.idx < b.idx ? a : b);
}
 
// We implement an iterative segment tree.
int main(){
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
 
    int n, m;
    cin >> n >> m;
    string a, b;
    cin >> a >> b;
 
    // Count '#' in string a.
    int r = 0;
    for(auto ch : a)
        if(ch == '#') r++;
    int L = m - r;  // m - r
 
    // If a has no '#' then nothing changes.
    if(r == 0){
        cout << a << "\n";
        return 0;
    }
 
    // Build array T: for i=1..m, T[i] = 'a' + ((i-1) mod 26).
    // We also initialize an array for the segment tree leaves: each leaf stores (letter, index).
    vector<Node> arr(m);

        char letter = 'a' + (i % 26);
        arr[i] = {letter, i+1}; // note: we use 1-indexed positions
    }
 
    // Build an iterative segment tree.
    int sizeTree = 1;
    while(sizeTree < m)
        sizeTree *= 2;

    for (int i = 0; i < m; i++){
        seg[sizeTree+i] = arr[i];

    for (int i = m; i < sizeTree; i++){
        seg[sizeTree+i] = {'{', INT_MAX};

    for (int i = sizeTree-1; i >= 1; i--){
        seg[i] = combine(seg[2*i], seg[2*i+1]);
    }
 
    // A lambda function to query the segment tree on interval [l, r] (here l,r are 1-indexed).
    auto querySeg = [&](int l, int r) -> Node {
        // convert to 0-indexed for seg tree leaves
        l = l - 1; r = r - 1;
        Node resL = {'{', INT_MAX}, resR = {'{', INT_MAX};
        l += sizeTree; r += sizeTree;

                l++;
            }
            if(r % 2 == 0){
                resR = combine(seg[r], resR);
                r--;
            }
            l /= 2; r /= 2;
        }
        return combine(resL, resR);
    };

    vector<int> chosen(r);
    int prev = 0;
    for (int j = 1; j <= r; j++){
        int low = prev + 1;
        int high = L + j;
        if(high > m) high = m;  // safeguard, though (L+j) should be ≤ m.
        Node best = querySeg(low, high);
        chosen[j-1] = best.idx;
        prev = best.idx;

In other words, you can “cancel out” the effect by pulling your hair back. But if you insist on letting long hair flow in the wind, you can expect an extra energy cost that might “cost” you on the order of 10 seconds in a top‐class marathon.)

Let’s walk through one plausible estimate.

1. Aerodynamic Drag Basics

For an object moving through air the drag force is
  F = (½) ρ v² C₍d₎ A
where
 ρ ≃ 1.2 kg/m³ is the air density,
 v is the speed,
 C₍d₎ the drag coefficient,
 A the “projected” area normal to the wind.

An elite marathoner runs roughly at v ≃ 6 m/s (about 22 km/h).

2. Extra “Hair‐drag”

Normally the body “presents” a frontal area of maybe about 0.5 m² (with Cd ~ 1 for a human “bluff body”). Most of the runner’s aerodynamic work comes from overcoming the drag on the torso/legs.
Let’s say that, if you sport long hair that flows loosely (say, hair reaching past the shoulders and allowed to flutter), the loose hair may “add” an extra effective area. Because hair is not a solid sheet (it’s limp and porous) its effective projected area is much less than its full extent and its effective drag coefficient may be lower than that of a flat plate. For our estimate we might assume:

  Effective hair area: A_h ≃ 0.02 m²  (a few square centimeters when “averaged” over flutter motions)
  Effective Cd for the hair: perhaps ~1 (if the hair is “flapping” randomly)

Then the extra drag force is

  F_hair = ½ · ρ · v² · C₍d,hair₎ · A_h 
      = ½ · 1.2 · (6²) · 1 · 0.02 
      ≃ 0.5 · 1.2 · 36 · 0.02 
      ≃ 0.5 · 0.864 
      ≃ 0.43 N.

Because power is force times velocity, the extra instantaneous power is

  P_hair = F_hair · v ≃ 0.43 N · 6 m/s ≃ 2.6 W.

An elite runner battling a marathon is expending power at maybe on the order of 300 W
(“300 W” here is a rough number for the mechanical work needed – note that the metabolic power is several times larger).
The “aerodynamic” part of that 300 W is not the whole story; when running slowly air‐resistance is only a fraction of the total cost. calculate how many seconds an Olympic marathon runner can expect to lose by having long hair (past shoulders) flowing in the wind

Below is one way of “back‐of‐the‐envelope” reasoning. (Keep in mind that the numbers that follow are subject to lots of uncertainties – hair is floppy, porous, and tends to “tuck in” when you run; real-world differences depend on how tightly one “ties one’s hair up” versus letting it flow. In other words, you can “cancel out” the effect by pulling your hair back. But if you insist on letting long hair flow in the wind, you can expect an extra energy cost that might “cost” you on the order of 10 seconds in a top‐class marathon.)

Let’s walk through one plausible estimate.

1. Aerodynamic Drag Basics

For an object moving through air the drag force is
  F = (½) ρ v² C₍d₎ A
where
 ρ ≃ 1.2 kg/m³ is the air density,
 v is the speed,
 C₍d₎ the drag coefficient,
 A the “projected” area normal to the wind.

An elite marathoner runs roughly at v ≃ 6 m/s (about 22 km/h).

2. Extra “Hair‐drag”

Normally the body “presents” a frontal area of maybe about 0.5 m² (with Cd ~ 1 for a human “bluff body”). Most of the runner’s aerodynamic work comes from overcoming the drag on the torso/legs.
Let’s say that, if you sport long hair that flows loosely (say, hair reaching past the shoulders and allowed to flutter), the loose hair may “add” an extra effective area. Because hair is not a solid sheet (it’s limp and porous) its effective projected area is much less than its full extent and its effective drag coefficient may be lower than that of a flat plate. For our estimate we might assume:

  Effective hair area: A_h ≃ 0.02 m²  (a few square centimeters when “averaged” over flutter motions)
  Effective Cd for the hair: perhaps ~1 (if the hair is “flapping” randomly)

Then the extra drag force is

  F_hair = ½ · ρ · v² · C₍d,hair₎ · A_h 
      = ½ · 1.2 · (6²) · 1 · 0.02 
      ≃ 0.5 · 1.2 · 36 · 0.02 
      ≃ 0.5 · 0.864 
      ≃ 0.43 N.

Because power is force times velocity, the extra instantaneous power is

  P_hair = F_hair · v ≃ 0.43 N · 6 m/s ≃ 2.6 W.

3. How Does This Translate into “Lost Seconds?”

An elite runner battling a marathon is expending power at maybe on the order of 300 W
(“300 W” here is a rough number for the mechanical work needed – note that the metabolic power is several times larger).
The “aerodynamic” part of that 300 W is not the whole story; when running slowly air‐resistance is only a fraction of the total cost. (For running at 6 m/s aerodynamic drag might cost something like 60–70 W, whereas the muscles must overcome internal losses, ground impacts, etc.) Nevertheless, if you compare the extra 2.6 W required to overcome the extra “hair‐drag” with, say, a body–drag power of roughly 65 W then the hair adds roughly a 4% increase in aerodynamic power.

Now, if you suppose that the “running economy” is such that (roughly speaking) every extra percent of power requirement ends up slowing you by a similar percent (if you have a fixed energy output per race), then a 4% extra aerodynamic power if aerodynamic work were the only extra cost would slow you by roughly 4% relative to that part of your effort. But here’s the catch: the aerodynamic cost may be only about 20% of your overall mechanical work. In that case the extra cost from hair is 4% × 20% = 0.8% of your overall energy expenditure.

What does 0.8% mean in elapsed race time? For a 2‐hour marathon (about 7200 seconds) that is

  0.008 × 7200 ≃ 58 seconds.

That number appears “large” by everyday standards. But note that many of the assumptions used are on the “pessimistic” side – if your hair actually “tucks in” or if aerodynamic forces on loose hair are partly “self–streamlining” (effective area or Cd drop from wobbling), the extra extra power might be only a fraction of 2.6 W. For example, if only 0.5–1 W extra is required (by having the hair “free‐flying”), then the overall effect might be to add on the order of 10–20 seconds to your race. (Different estimates on exactly which number to “trust” abound.)

4. A “Rounded” Estimate

After playing with the numbers one might conclude that the extra power requirement could be on the order of 1–3 W. In “real‐world” terms the penalty for leaving your long hair to “fly free” might be somewhere between 5 and 20 seconds over an Olympic marathon—that is, compared to the ideal “tied–up” configuration.

A “typical” back-of-the-envelope answer might be: approximately 10 seconds lost due to the extra drag from long, flowy hair.

5. Caveats

• These estimates depend on many assumptions:
 – What is the effective area and drag coefficient of “flowing hair”?
 – What fraction of your metabolic energy is allocated to overcoming aerodynamic drag?
• Elite runners can “adjust” their form (by tying hair back, wearing a cap, or tucking hair into a headband) so that in practice the actual wasted energy due to hair free–flapping will be considerably lower than this worst-case estimate.
• In any event, the extra “hair‐drag” is very small compared not only with the overall forces involved in running but also with many other sources of variability in marathon performance.

Final Answer

Under plausible assumptions the extra aerodynamic “penalty” from long hair free–flapping might be on the order of 10 seconds (give or take a few seconds) over a full Olympic–level marathon.

So, roughly speaking, if an Olympic marathoner elected not to tie back long, shoulder–past hair, they might lose about 10 seconds due to the extra drag.

from pulp import *
import random

def generate_coverage(strategy_id):
    """
    根据策略ID生成覆盖区域。
    :param strategy_id: 策略的类型ID
    :return: 覆盖区域的坐标偏移列表
    """
    if  strategy_id == 1:
        return [(i, j) for i in range(-1, 2) for j in range(-1, 2)] # 3x3
    elif strategy_id == 2:
        return [(i, j) for i in range(-2, 2) for j in range(-1, 2)] # 4x3
    elif strategy_id == 3:
        return [(i, j) for i in range(-2, 3) for j in range(-2, 3)] # 5x5
    elif strategy_id == 4:
        return [(0, j) for j in range(-6, 7)] # 全列覆盖
    elif strategy_id == 5:
        return [(i, 0) for i in range(-8, 9)] # 全行覆盖
    elif strategy_id == 6:
        return [(0, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)] # 小十字
    elif strategy_id == 7:
        return [(i, j) for j in range(-1, 2) for i in range(-8, 9)] # 三行覆盖
    else:
        raise ValueError("未知的策略ID")
def generate_cross_coverage(rows, cols):
    """
    根据给定的行数和列数生成十字覆盖范围。
    :param rows: 十字的行数
    :param cols: 十字的列数
    :return: 覆盖区域的坐标偏移列表
    """
    coverage = []
    # 纵向覆盖
    for i in range(-rows, rows + 1):
        coverage.append((i, 0))
    # 横向覆盖
    for j in range(-cols, cols + 1):
        coverage.append((0, j))
    return coverage

def add_strategy(strategies, strategy_id, cost, rows=None, cols=None):
    """

    :param strategies: 策略字典
    :param strategy_id: 策略的类型ID
    :param cost: 策略的成本
    :param rows: 十字的行数（仅用于十字策略）
    :param cols: 十字的列数（仅用于十字策略）
    """
    global strategy_count
    strategy_count += 1 # 增加计数器

    if strategy_id == 8:

    # 添加策略到字典，使用唯一ID

    add_strategy(strategies, 1, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 2, 2275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 4, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 6, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 2, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 2, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 3, 2375)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 4, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 5, 275)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 7, 25)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 8, 325,2,2)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 8, 275,3,5)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 8, 2735,2,4)  # 5x5
    add_strategy(strategies, 9, 325)  # 复制策略
    add_strategy(strategies, 3, 325)  # 复制策略
    add_strategy(strategies, 2, 13)  # 复制策略
    add_strategy(strategies, 2, 12)  # 复制策略
    add_strategy(strategies, 4, 8)  # 复制策略
    add_strategy(strategies, 6, 6)  # 复制策略
    add_strategy(strategies, 7, 10)  # 复制策略


    # 创建决策变量
    x = LpVariable.dicts("strategy",
                         [(i, j, s) for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1)
                          for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)
                          for s in strategies.keys()],
                         cat='Binary')

                                         [(i, j, s, str(strategy_count)) for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1)
                                          for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)
                                          for s in strategies.keys() if s != str(strategy_count)],
                                         cat='Binary')

    # 目标函数
    prob += lpSum([strategies[s]["cost"] * x[i, j, s] for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1)
                   for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)
                   for s in strategies.keys()])

    # 约束条件

                                         for j_s in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)
                                         for s in strategies.keys() if s != str(strategy_count)
                                         if (i - i_s, j - j_s) in strategies[s]["coverage"]])

                                              for j_s in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)
                                              for s in strategies.keys() if s != str(strategy_count)
                                              if (i - i_s, j - j_s) in strategies[s]["coverage"]])

            prob += coverage_constraint >= 1

    for obstacle in obstacles:
        i, j = map(int, obstacle.split('-'))
        for s in strategies.keys():
            prob += x[i, j, s] == 0

    # 3. 每个策略只能被放置一次
    for s in strategies.keys():
        prob += lpSum([x[i, j, s] for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1)
                       for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)]) <= 1

        if consider_copy_strategy:
            # 确保复制策略只复制一个其他策略
            for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1):
                for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1):
                    prob += lpSum([copy_coverage[i, j, s, str(strategy_count)]
                                   for s in strategies.keys() if s != str(strategy_count)]) == x[i, j, str(strategy_count)]

            # 确保只有在原策略被使用时才能复制
            for s in strategies.keys():
                if s != str(strategy_count):
                    prob += lpSum([copy_coverage[i, j, s, str(strategy_count)]
                                   for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1)
                                   for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)]) <= lpSum([x[i_s, j_s, s]
                                                                                 for i_s in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1)
                                                                                 for j_s in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1)])

    # 求解问题
    prob.solve()

# 输出结果
    print("Status:", LpStatus[prob.status])
    if LpStatus[prob.status] == "Optimal":  # 有解
        print("火苗花费 =", value(prob.objective))

        # 存储复制策略的信息

            if s != str(strategy_count):  # 不是复制策略
                for i in range(1, MAP_WIDTH + 1):
                    for j in range(1, MAP_HEIGHT + 1):
                        if value(x[i, j, s]) > 0.99:
                            print(f"对策卡 {s} 放置于 ({i},{j})")

                            # 检查是否有复制这个策略的复制策略

                        break  # 找到策略放置位置后跳出外层循环

    else:
        print("问题无解")
# 定义待处理点位列表

    若待检测点相对于放置点 (i_s, j_s) 所形成的偏移量在该策略 s 的覆盖区域内，则该放置点能覆盖该点  
   – 若考虑复制策略，会将标准策略和复制策略的贡献都考虑进去  
   – 最终为每个待覆盖点添加不小于1的约束

  2. 障碍约束  
   – 对障碍点（坐标由 obstacles 列表给定）不允许放置任何策略，所以对所有策略 s 强制 x[i, j, s] == 0

  3. “每个策略只能放置一次”约束  
   – 对每个策略 s，地图上所有位置放置该策略的组合和小于等于1  
   – 针对复制策略（如果考虑复制策略），增加两个额外约束：  
    a. 每个地图位置上复制策略变量 copy_coverage[i,j,s,s_copy] 的累加值等于在同一位置放置复制策略（x[i,j,复制策略]）  
    b. 只有当原策略被放置时，才能将其复制——通过对所有位置上放置该策略的 x 求和，与复制变量求和之间的关系限定

  – 调用 prob.solve() 求解问题，然后输出求解状态以及目标函数值（总代价）  
  – 若求解为 Optimal，则遍历所有非复制策略 s，在地图上寻找 x[i,j,s] 为1 的位置，输出该策略卡的位置信息  
  – 同时对复制策略（ID为 strategy_count 的策略）检查是否复制了某一策略，如果在相关位置 x 与 copy_coverage 均为1，则输出复制信息

─────────────────────────────  
【4. 调用与输入数据】

在代码末尾定义了两个列表：  
  – points_to_cover：待覆盖的点，坐标使用 “行-列” 格式（如 "9-5"）  
  – obstacles：表示障碍位置，放置策略时不能在这些点上放置  
此外，变量 consider_copy_strategy 控制是否考虑复制策略的约束（此处设置为 True）。

─────────────────────────────  
【5. 总结】

• 这份代码利用 PuLP 构建了一个整数规划问题，用于在 9×7 的地图上以最小成本放置各种对策卡，确保所有指定的点得到覆盖，同时考虑了障碍、策略不同位置的覆盖能力，以及复制策略的特殊要求。  
• 各个策略的覆盖区域由生成函数（generate_coverage、generate_cross_coverage）确定，覆盖检查时只要点相对于策略放置坐标呈现的偏移量存在于策略的覆盖区域中，即认为该放置策略能够“覆盖”该点。
